app.tagline: Finds and fixes what Radarr and Sonarr leave lying around

page.settings: Services, notifications, checks, paths and appearance

page.activity: What was found and what was done
page.downloads: On their way in, scored against today's rules

topbar.check_deep_help: Downloads, library and indexers — takes longer

dry.remove: would take it out of the queue
dry.blocklist_and_search: would blocklist it and search again
dry.import_and_clean: would import it and clear the download client entry
dry.remove_entry: would remove the entry and its source folder
dry.unblocklist: would take it off the blocklist and search again
dry.retune_profile: would stop the profile upgrading on score
dry.as_suggested: would do what the finding suggests

result.already_gone: it had already left the queue — imported or removed, nothing left to do
result.folder_cleared_searched: source folder cleared, new search started
result.imported_partly: {count} file(s) imported, {skipped} skipped because the service did not say which episodes they hold
result.matched_imported_cleaned: matched and imported ({gb} GB), {client} cleaned up
result.entry_removed: entry and source folder removed ({gb} GB)
result.unblocklisted_searched: taken off the blocklist, new search started

home.all_good_text: Nothing is waiting for you. Correctarr keeps checking in the background.
home.waiting_text: Found, and deliberately not dealt with by itself. Most of them take a single press.
home.no_services_text: Connect Radarr or Sonarr and Correctarr starts checking.
home.dry_run_on: Dry run is on: problems are reported, nothing is changed.
home.storage_text: How much is free, how fast it fills, and when it is full.

overview.decisions_deletes: {count} would delete — those are decided one by one.
overview.cleanup_none: No cleanup directory configured — the leftover files rule stays quiet.

fixed_page.help: Only changes that actually happened — plain reports and dry runs are not listed here. This is the record of the work done.
fixed_page.empty: Nothing has been changed yet. That is good news to start with.

findings_page.decide_help: Each of these was found and deliberately not dealt with by itself. The first button is what is recommended; everything else the rule can do sits beside it.
findings_page.decide_empty: Nothing is waiting for you. Everything found so far was either dealt with or needs no decision.
findings_page.dismiss_help: Leave it alone and hide it until it changes. It stays in the log.
findings_page.undismissed_toast: It is back in the list.
findings_page.fix_all_recommended: Do what is recommended for all {count}
findings_page.fix_all_recommended_help: Each one gets its own recommendation — for exactly what is in the list right now.
findings_page.left_for_you: {count} that would delete are left for you.

activity.log_help: Everything the checks found, newest first. Open a line for the details.
activity.resolution_help: A problem counts as resolved once no check comes across it any more — whether it was fixed here, in the service, or went away by itself.

queue_page.help: A release is scored only once, when it is grabbed. This view re-scores every waiting entry against the rules that apply today. A large gap between "then" and "now" means the profile changed after the grab.

rules_page.confirm_report_only: Set every rule to report only? Problems will still be found, but nothing will be changed.
rules_page.confirm_defaults: Reset every rule to its default?
rules_page.report_only_done: Every rule is now set to report only
rules_page.intro: Every rule checks one kind of problem. Switched off, it does not run at all; the choice beside it decides what happens when it finds something.
rules_page.conditions_when_acting: Conditions can be set once the rule does more than report.
rules_page.all_at_once_help: Report only stops every rule from changing anything; the defaults bring back what each rule does out of the box.

indexers_page.help: Prowlarr knows how often an indexer was queried and how often that turned into a grab. Radarr and Sonarr know how good the grab was. Together that makes the rating. Nothing is changed here — a wrongly set priority is easy to make and hard to notice later.
indexers_page.none: No Prowlarr configured — add one under Services.
indexers_page.deviation: Ranked {actual} by configuration, {target} by measurement — priority {priority} would be better at {suggested}
indexers_page.not_rated: Too little data for a rating yet.
indexers_page.how: How the rating is worked out

library.reading: Reading the libraries — the first time this can take a few seconds.
library.no_services: Connect Radarr or Sonarr to see how the disks are doing.
library.incomplete: Not every library on this disk has enough history yet, so it will probably be full sooner.
library.read_partly: The files of {read} of {total} series were read one by one; the rest are counted as a whole.
library.profiles_title: Profiles and their price on the disk
library.profiles_text: What each profile will take, and moving titles between them.

services_page.help: Radarr, Sonarr, SABnzbd and Prowlarr. Each Arr service can get a webhook connection so it reports the moment it grabs something or needs manual work. That requires the public address of this interface under Settings.
services_page.key_hint: Leave the placeholder as it is to keep the stored key.
services_page.key_where: Found in the service under Settings → General.
services_page.key_again: Enter the API key again for the new address

settings_page.group_schedule_help: How often things are checked. The fast pass only walks the queue and takes seconds; the deep pass additionally walks the whole library and the indexers.
settings_page.group_safety_help: The limits every automatic action has to pass, whichever rule asks for it. They exist so that a rule that is wrong about something cannot be wrong about it over and over. Actions taken with a button are counted but never blocked.
settings_page.group_paths_help: Where the files are, as seen from inside this container rather than from the host. They have to match the mounts Radarr, Sonarr and the download client see.
settings_page.group_detection_help: The thresholds at which a rule reacts. Higher means more cautious: fewer findings, but safer ones.
settings_page.group_cleanup_help: The only rule that deletes irreversibly. It deletes only when every condition holds at once — and never without a reachable download client.
settings_page.group_indexers_help: Indexer rating is read only. Nothing is changed, only suggested.
settings_page.group_notifications_help: Reports are bundled at the end of a run, never sent one by one.
settings_page.group_appearance_help: How the interface looks and where it can be reached.
settings_page.group_maintenance_help: How long findings are kept. Without a limit the store grows without bound.
settings_page.theme_help: Every theme is dark — this runs next to Radarr and Sonarr, and so are they.
settings_page.compact_help: Applies the limits from the Maintenance group immediately.
settings_page.account_disabled: Authentication is disabled through AUTH=off. There is no account to manage — and the interface is reachable by anyone who can reach the port.
settings_page.sessions_note: All other sessions will be ended.
settings_page.rerun_setup_help: Walks through services, paths, the callback address and notifications again. Nothing is reset.
settings_page.webhook_title: How Radarr and Sonarr reach Correctarr

backup_ui.title: Backup and restore
backup_ui.help: Every setting, what every rule is set to do, the services and the notification connections, as one file.
backup_ui.secrets_note: Keep a file like that somewhere safe: anyone who has it can control your services.
backup_ui.restore_help: Pick a backup file. You see what it would change before anything is written, and nothing that is not in the file is removed.
backup_ui.nothing: This backup matches what is set up now — there is nothing to change.
backup_ui.webhooks: The webhooks of {names} still point at the installation the backup came from. Save each of them once under Services to set them up here.

setup.intro: Create the account you will sign in with from now on. Services come next.
setup.warning: The password can only be changed through this interface later. There is no way to reset it without access to the file under /config.
setup.password_help: At least 8 characters. Length matters more than special characters.
setup.mismatch: The two passwords do not match.
setup.external_auth: Running behind your own authentication, such as Authelia or Authentik? Then this one can be turned off with the environment variable AUTH=off.

path.unset_required: Without this path the file rules stay inactive.
path.unset_optional: Not set — fine if that folder does not exist.
path.missing: {path} does not exist inside this container. Is the mount missing?
path.read_only: read only, cleanup will not work
path.write_needed: write access is needed here, because {rules} may delete

run.already_running: A run is already in progress

message.password_changed: Password changed. Other sessions have been ended.
message.webhook_needs_url: Webhook skipped: the public address of this interface is missing under Settings, Appearance.

notify.title: {count} new finding(s)
notify.test_body: This is a test message. If you are reading it, the connection works.

error.password_whitespace: The password must not start or end with a space.
error.password_is_username: The password and the username must not be the same.

error.rule_cannot_fix: "{name}" cannot fix anything — the rule only reports.
error.url_scheme: The address has to start with http:// or https://
error.url_scheme_https: The address has to start with https://
error.api_key_again: The address has changed — enter the API key again, so the stored one is not sent somewhere new
error.foreign_origin: Refused: this request came from another web page
error.no_services: No service is configured. Add at least Radarr or Sonarr under Services.
error.already_running: A run is already in progress
error.unknown_field_kind: Internal: a setting is declared with an unknown kind ({value}).
error.no_connections: There is no notification connection to send to.
error.backup_unreadable: This is not a Correctarr backup.
error.backup_too_new: This backup was made by a newer version of Correctarr. Update first.
error.no_such_finding: That finding is no longer in the log.
error.nothing_to_do: There is nothing this rule can do about it.
error.no_connection: The server cannot be reached. Is the container running?
error.signed_out: You have been signed out. Please sign in again.
error.invalid_input: Some of what was sent is not valid. Check the fields and try again.
error.server: The server ran into a problem (error {status}). The container log says more.
error.service_said: The service answered with an error: {text}

reason.archives_only: archive remnants only ({count} files, nothing unpacked)

finding.wrong_year: The release says {found}, but the title is from {expected}. That is a different item.
finding.wrong_title: The release name resembles none of the {count} known titles for this item (best match {percent}). Probably matched to the wrong thing.
finding.profile_violation: Under today's rules of "{profile}" this release is blocked: {reason}. It was grabbed before the rule existed.
finding.not_an_upgrade: Not an upgrade over the existing file. It will never be imported.
finding.grab_loop: {count} grabs in {hours} hours. Probably no available release satisfies the profile — that can only be solved in the profile.

stuck.client_unavailable: The download client has not been reachable for {hours} h. Nothing is done to the download while it cannot be asked. The service says: {text}
stuck.not_grabbed: In the queue for {hours} h, but not grabbed by the service — somebody else's download, left alone. The service says: {text}
stuck.path_problem: Stuck for {hours} h on a path or disk problem — a folder the service cannot see, a missing remote path mapping, missing permissions or a full disk. Blocklisting would not help. The service says: {text}
stuck.failed: Failed {hours} h ago and already handled by the service, but still in the queue. Can be removed. The service says: {text}
stuck.failed_pending: The download failed {hours} h ago and the service has not dealt with it. Blocklist and search again. The service says: {text}
stuck.already_imported: Already imported, still in the queue after {hours} h. Can be removed. The service says: {text}
stuck.not_an_upgrade: Would not be an upgrade and has been waiting {hours} h. Blocklist. The service says: {text}
stuck.sample: Only a sample, or a file the service cannot measure, for {hours} h. Probably broken — blocklist and search again? The service says: {text}
stuck.no_files: Finished {hours} h ago with nothing in it that can be imported. Blocklist and search again. The service says: {text}
stuck.matched_by_id: Waiting for {hours} h: the grab history names the title, but the release name does not quite agree, so the service will not import it by itself. Import if the release is right. The service says: {text}
stuck.unknown_item: Waiting for {hours} h: the service cannot tell which title this is. The service says: {text}
stuck.missing_episodes: Waiting for {hours} h: some episodes the release should contain are missing or were not imported. Import what is there? The service says: {text}
stuck.tba_title: Waiting for {hours} h for an episode title that is still TBA. Import anyway? The service says: {text}
stuck.manual: Waiting for {hours} h for a manual import. The service says: {text}
stuck.import_pending: Waiting for {hours} h to be imported without saying why. Import? The service says: {text}
stuck.importing: Importing for {hours} h — that normally takes minutes. The service says: {text}
stuck.other: Stuck for {hours} h in a state nothing else here knows. The service says: {text}
stuck.dl_paused: Paused on its own in {client} for {hours} h while everything else runs. Resume? {text}
stuck.dl_encrypted: {client} paused this {hours} h ago because it is encrypted. It cannot be unpacked — blocklist and search again. {text}
stuck.dl_unwanted: {client} paused this {hours} h ago because it carries an unwanted file type. Blocklist and search again. {text}
stuck.dl_fetching: {client} has been fetching this for {hours} h without starting. {text}
stuck.dl_postprocessing: {client} has been post-processing this for {hours} h — that normally takes minutes. {text}
stuck.dl_failed_unnoticed: {client} gave up on this {hours} h ago and the service that grabbed it never noticed — often a changed category. Blocklist and search again. {text}
stuck.dl_completed_unclaimed: Finished in {client} {hours} h ago, and the service that grabbed it never picked it up — usually a category or path mismatch. Import? {text}

finding.manual_import: Manual work is being demanded although the title and year line up.
finding.unpack_failed: Unpacking failed: no usable video file, untouched for {hours} hours, and the download client no longer knows the job.
finding.detached_folder: {service} reports {count} file(s) in {path}, but the same folder looks empty here. Almost always the path mapping: this container's {path} points to a different folder on the host than the one {service} and the download client use. Map it to the same host folder in the container settings — until then nothing in the download folder can be checked or cleaned up. Less often, the folder was recreated on the host while a container held it mounted; then restarting that container fixes it.
finding.unmatched_importable: The file is not matched to any title, {reason}. Importing it would be an improvement ({comparison}).
finding.unmatched_no_gain: A match is possible ({reason}), but importing would be no improvement ({comparison}). Left alone.
finding.unmatched_giving_up: Cannot be matched to any title: {reason}. It has been sitting for {hours} hours — the release will be blocklisted and searched for again.
finding.unmatched_waiting: Cannot be matched to any title: {reason}. It has been sitting for {hours} hours, still waiting.
finding.cleanup_no_paths: No cleanup directory is configured. Set the finished and incomplete download paths under Settings, Paths.
finding.cleanup_no_downloader: No download client is configured. Without comparing against its queue nothing is classified as debris — a folder can be untouched for hours and be perfectly fine. Add a SABnzbd entry under Services.
finding.cleanup_downloader_down: The download client is not answering. Without comparing against its queue nothing is classified as debris — a folder can be untouched for hours and be perfectly fine.
finding.leftover_files: {reason}, untouched for {days} days, {mb} MB. Neither the download client nor the Arr services know it any more.
finding.missing_audio_language: The existing file has none of the wanted audio languages (found: {found}, wanted: {wanted}).
finding.unreadable_file: No media information could be read from this file. That points at a damaged or incomplete file.
finding.below_profile: Under today's rules of "{profile}" the existing file would be blocked: {reason}.
finding.missing_items: Monitored, released in {year}, and there is no file. Nothing will look for one until a search is started.
finding.downloader_stale_entry: The file is already in the library as "{title}" ({gb} GB). The entry in {client} can go, along with its source folder.
finding.downloader_paused: The download client is paused while {waiting} entries are waiting. Nothing is arriving although grabbing continues.
finding.indexer_disabled: Prowlarr has switched the indexer off until {until} because of errors. Last error: {last_error}.
finding.indexer_ineffective: {queries} queries, only {grabs} grabs out of them ({percent} percent). The indexer costs time and quota on every search and contributes nothing.
finding.indexer_ranking: Ranked {actual} by configuration, {target} by measurement (rating {rating}). Priority {actual_priority} would be better at {suggested}.
finding.indexer_unknown: The indexer shows up in the history (mean score {score}) but Prowlarr does not know it. Either it is configured directly in the Arr service, or it has since been removed from Prowlarr.
finding.disk_space: Only {free} GB free out of {total} GB.
finding.premature_grab: Not out until {date}, which is {days} days away. There is no honest copy of this yet.
finding.cutoff_unmet: On disk as {quality}. The profile “{profile}” keeps upgrading until {cutoff}, so this is not what was asked for — but nothing goes looking for a better copy on its own.
finding.season_gaps: {missing} of {total} episodes of season {season} are missing, and the rest are there. A season pack that imported partly, or episodes that failed and were never noticed.
finding.series_incomplete: The series has finished airing and {missing} of {total} episodes are still missing. This will not fix itself.
finding.stale_blocklist: Blocklisted {days} days ago: {release}. The title is still missing, so this refusal may be the reason.
finding.stray_files: {gb} GB in this folder that {service} does not know about: {archives} archive parts, {videos} other videos, {samples} samples, {leftovers} files of an unfinished download or unpack.
finding.stray_samples: {count} sample video(s) still lying beside the title, {mb} MB. {service} does not know about them.
finding.stray_files_hidden: None of the folders {service} keeps its titles in can be seen from here, so nothing in them could be checked. Mount the library into this container — read only is enough — and set it under Settings, Paths (now {path}).
finding.missing_episodes: {count} episode(s) of season {season} are missing ({episodes}). Monitored and aired, with no file — nothing will look for them until a search is started.
finding.cutoff_unmet_season: {count} episode(s) of season {season} ({episodes}) are on disk as {quality}. The profile “{profile}” keeps upgrading until {cutoff}. Nothing goes looking for a better copy on its own.
finding.missing_nothing_out_there: Searched on {tries} separate occasions since {since} and nothing turned up. It looks like this simply is not available anywhere your indexers can see. Nothing further will be searched for by itself.
finding.missing_episodes_nothing_out_there: {count} episode(s) of season {season} ({episodes}) are still missing after searches on {tries} separate occasions since {since}. It looks like they are not out there. Nothing further will be searched for by itself.
finding.cutoff_nothing_better: On disk as {quality}. The profile “{profile}” would like {cutoff}, but searches on {tries} separate occasions since {since} have turned up nothing better — this is probably the best copy there is. Nothing further will be searched for by itself.
finding.collection_pack: This is not one film, it is the set: {reason} ({span}), {gb} GB. Radarr cannot import that — it downloads all of them and then fails, or takes the wrong one.
finding.collection_pack_no_span: This is not one film, it is the set: {reason}, {gb} GB. Radarr cannot import that — it downloads all of them and then fails, or takes the wrong one.
finding.profile_loop_unreachable: Keeps upgrading until a file scores {target}, and the best of the last {samples} grabs scored {best}. Nothing out there reaches the target, so every one of its {titles} titles is permanently “not good enough yet” and gets fetched again.
finding.profile_loop_repeating: Keeps upgrading until a file scores {target}, and {repeats} title(s) under it have been fetched three times or more. A target above zero is a bet that a file keeps its score after import — it does not.
finding.profile_loop_risk: Keeps upgrading until a file scores {target}. Nothing has looped yet, but any target above zero can: a file often scores less after import than its release did.
finding.profile_loop_set_back: Was corrected to 0 and has been set back to {target} since. Another program maintains this profile — in Profilarr, set “upgrade until score” to 0 in the profile itself, or it will be overwritten again.
finding.profile_cutoff_disabled: Stops upgrading at a quality the profile does not allow, so it can never stop. The service searches for it for good.
finding.profile_floor_unreachable: A release needs at least {floor} points to be grabbed, and the most any release can score under this profile is {reachable}. Nothing will ever be grabbed.

wrong_year.title: Year does not match the title
wrong_year.help: Blocklists the release and searches again immediately. Names without a year are left alone — there is nothing to compare.

wrong_title.title: Release name resembles no known title
wrong_title.help: Compares against localised distribution titles as well — otherwise every translated release would be a false alarm. Those titles only exist in the full item list, so this rule runs in the deep pass only.

profile_violation.title: Download breaks today's profile rules
profile_violation.help: Re-scores waiting downloads against the rules that apply now. Also catches 3D releases that Radarr cannot detect itself, because its parser swallows markers placed before the year.

not_an_upgrade.title: Import would not be an upgrade
not_an_upgrade.help: Blocklists the release without searching again — the existing file is better after all.

stalled.title: A started download stopped moving
stalled.help: Only downloads that started and then stopped. Entries that have not begun are normal and are never reported.

grab_loop.title: The same title is grabbed over and over
grab_loop.help: Reports only: the cause sits in the profile, and that is where it has to be fixed.

stuck_in_queue.title: Download stuck in the queue
stuck_in_queue.help: The net under every other queue rule: anything the service has marked as blocked, pending, failed or with a warning for longer than the configured time. The finding carries the service's own words and the remedy they call for. Only certain remedies are carried out unasked — a dead download is replaced, one already in the library is tidied away; an import on weaker evidence than the service had is offered as a button.

manual_import.title: Import waiting on manual work, but the match is right
manual_import.help: Imports only when BOTH the year and the title similarity check out. Everything else belongs to the wrong year and wrong title rules.

unpack_failed.title: Unpacking really failed
unpack_failed.help: An _UNPACK_ folder is normal at first — that is what it is called WHILE unpacking. Only reported when it is old enough, holds no video, and the download client no longer knows the job.

detached_folder.title: Service and container see different download folders
detached_folder.help: Compares what the service reports in the download folder with what this container sees there. Usually means the container's download path is mapped to a different host folder than the service's; less often that the folder was recreated while a container held it mounted.

leftover_files.title: Leftover download debris
leftover_files.help: Deletes half RAR sets, empty and failed folders. It deletes only what satisfies EVERY condition: old enough, no longer tracked by the download client, in no Arr queue, no usable video inside, and within the configured directories. If the download client is unreachable, nothing is deleted at all.

unmatched_files.title: File without a match — matches it itself
unmatched_files.help: The parser trips over small things such as Roman numerals ("Crank.I" for "Crank 1") or a leading "The". The matching here handles those and compares against every alternate title. It imports only on an unambiguous match with a fitting year AND when it would be an improvement.

missing_audio_language.title: Existing file lacks the wanted audio language
missing_audio_language.help: Checked against the real audio tracks of the file, not the file name — the most reliable language evidence there is. Does nothing until you name the languages you want.

unreadable_file.title: File cannot be read
unreadable_file.help: Missing media information points at a damaged file. Fixed by rescanning it.

below_profile.title: Existing file would be blocked today
below_profile.help: Reports only substantive violations such as 3D, mic dubs, AAC or Xvid. Pure size shortfalls are left out — they affect almost the whole library and say nothing about its quality.

missing_items.title: Monitored and released, but no file
missing_items.help: Reports only — a bulk search can cost a lot of disk space.

downloader_warning.title: The download client is reporting a warning
downloader_warning.help: Records the warning and then clears it, so it does not sit there forever. The cause itself — a broken NZB, say — is resolved by the service searching again.

downloader_stale_entry.title: Entry finished, file long since imported
downloader_stale_entry.help: After a manual import the download client never finds out — the entry and its source folder stay. Detected by a file size matching to within one percent AND by the title; size alone is not enough, several films happen to be the same size.

downloader_paused.title: The download client is paused
downloader_paused.help: Easy to miss for a long time: the queue grows but nothing arrives. Deliberately set to report only — a pause is often intentional.

downloader_disk_space.title: The download client is reporting little free space

downloader_update.title: A new version of the download client is available
downloader_update.help: SABnzbd is reporting a newer version of itself. Worth knowing, nothing more — updating is up to you.

stuck_in_downloader.title: Job stuck in the download client
stuck_in_downloader.help: What the services cannot see: a job paused on its own because it is encrypted or carries an unwanted file, one fetching or post-processing for hours, one that failed or finished without the service that grabbed it ever noticing. Matched by download id against the services' grab history; a job no service grabbed is left alone. Deep pass only.

indexer_disabled.title: Prowlarr has switched an indexer off
indexer_disabled.help: Takes effect immediately: every search reaches one source fewer.

indexer_ineffective.title: Indexer delivers nothing despite many queries
indexer_ineffective.help: Costs time and quota. Reported only — it may cover a rare niche.

indexer_ranking.title: The order contradicts the measured usefulness
indexer_ranking.help: Rating made of yield (40%), quality of the grabs (35%), reliability (15%) and speed (10%). A suggestion only — nothing is changed.

indexer_unknown.title: Indexer bypasses Prowlarr
indexer_unknown.help: Either configured directly in the Arr service, or removed from Prowlarr since.

service_health.title: The service reports a problem about itself
service_health.help: Passes the health messages from Radarr and Sonarr through.

disk_space.title: Free space is running low
disk_space.help: Only looks at the locations configured as root folders.

api_changes.title: Part of the API is being replaced
api_changes.help: The service marked one of the calls this makes as on its way out. It still works, and will for a while. This is the only advance warning available, and it names exactly what needs changing before it stops.

premature_grab.title: A release for something that is not out yet
premature_grab.help: Reports only. An early release in one region is rare but real, and being wrong here throws away the only copy there is.

cutoff_unmet.title: Present, but below the quality that was asked for
cutoff_unmet.help: Reports only — searching for every title below its cutoff at once is a great many indexer queries.

season_gaps.title: A season that is only partly there
season_gaps.help: Sonarr only. Costs nothing to ask: the counts arrive with the series list.

series_incomplete.title: A finished series that is still incomplete
series_incomplete.help: Sonarr only. A running series missing last week is waiting; one that ended four years ago is missing it permanently.

stale_blocklist.title: An old refusal that may be why a title never arrives
stale_blocklist.help: Only raised where the title is still missing. A blocklisted release for something that has since arrived is doing its job.

stray_files.title: Files in a title's folder that the service knows nothing about
stray_files.help: Archive parts, half-unpacked downloads, sample videos and other videos lying in the folder of a film or series beside the files the service holds for it. Report only: the library is mounted read only on purpose, and a video that is not the title's own file may be the only copy of something else. Subtitles, artwork and .nfo files are left alone, and so are extras in the folders Plex and Jellyfin read them from. Needs the library under Settings, Paths.

collection_pack.title: A box set, when one film was asked for
collection_pack.help: Blocklists it and searches again straight away. Only above 80 % certainty by default, because it throws a download away — every signal is measured against the film's own title, so a year in the title does not count against it.

profile_loop.title: A quality profile that makes the service fetch the same thing again
profile_loop.help: Measured against the grabs the service has actually made. Stops the profile upgrading on score, which ends the loop and leaves resolution upgrades alone. If a profile manager such as Profilarr sets it back, it says so instead of fighting it.

fast_seconds.label: Check the queue every
fast_seconds.help: The fast pass. Walks the queue only and takes a few seconds. It cannot be set below 20 seconds — the Arr services have work to do as well.

deep_minutes.label: Check the library every
deep_minutes.help: The deep pass walks every title and the indexers. On large libraries that takes noticeably longer.

event_debounce.label: Minimum gap after an event
event_debounce.help: Bundles webhook calls: several in quick succession trigger a single pass. Without it a search wave would start a hundred passes in parallel.

events_enabled.label: React to webhooks
events_enabled.help: Radarr and Sonarr report the moment they grab something or need manual work. Off means checks happen on the schedule only.

dry_run.label: Dry run
dry_run.help: On: problems are found and reported, but nothing is changed. The safe way to try out a new setting.

safety_title_limit.label: Act on the same title at most
safety_title_limit.help: How often one film, episode, profile or folder may be acted on within the window below, across every rule. Past that the finding is still reported, but left for a person: something is going round in a circle.

safety_title_hours.label: …within
safety_title_hours.help: The window the limit above counts in. A title that was thrown out and then grabbed again is held for this long, too.

safety_hourly_limit.label: Pause everything after, per hour
safety_hourly_limit.help: More automatic actions than this within an hour, and all of them stop until you resume them by hand. A notification goes out when it happens, and a restart does not undo it.

safety_discard_limit.label: Pause everything after, per hour, of those that throw something away
safety_discard_limit.help: The same, counted only over removing, blocklisting and deleting. These are the ones that make the service fetch something else, which is how a loop starts.

path_downloads.label: Finished downloads
path_downloads.help: The folder the download client puts finished downloads in. It has to be the same one Radarr and Sonarr see.

path_incomplete.label: Incomplete downloads
path_incomplete.help: The working folder of the download client. Leave empty if there is no separate one.

extra_cleanup_paths.label: Additional cleanup directories
extra_cleanup_paths.help: One path per line. Finished and incomplete downloads are included automatically and do not need to be listed here.

year_tolerance.label: Year tolerance
year_tolerance.help: How far the year may differ before a release counts as the wrong item. One year is sensible: cinema and home release often fall either side of new year.

title_similarity.label: Minimum title similarity
title_similarity.help: Below this a release name counts as not matching the title. 0.45 is a good compromise — localised distribution titles differ a lot.

stalled_minutes.label: Stalled after
stalled_minutes.help: When a started download counts as stuck. Downloads that have not begun are normal and never reported.

stuck_hours.label: A download counts as stuck after
stuck_hours.help: How long a queue entry or download client job may sit in a waiting or failed state before it is reported. The services retry imports every minute, so hours rather than minutes.

loop_grabs.label: Grabs before it counts as a loop
loop_grabs.help: How often the same title may be grabbed before it is worth mentioning.

loop_hours.label: Window for counting grabs
loop_hours.help: Grabs are counted within this period.

disk_threshold_gb.label: Warn when free space drops below
disk_threshold_gb.help: Below half of this it is reported as an error rather than a warning.

give_up_hours.label: Give up on an unmatched file after
give_up_hours.help: How long to wait before an unmatchable release is blocklisted and searched for again. 0 disables giving up — the file then stays where it is.

unpack_timeout_hours.label: Unpacking counts as failed after
unpack_timeout_hours.help: An _UNPACK_ folder is entirely normal at first — that is what the download client calls a folder while it is unpacking. It is only reported once it is this old, holds no video, and the client no longer knows the job.

downloader_done_hours.label: Check finished entries after
downloader_done_hours.help: How long a completed entry has to sit in the download client before it is checked against the library.

audio_languages.label: Wanted audio languages
audio_languages.help: Comma separated, for example "German, English". Names and codes mean the same: "de", "ger" and "deu" are all German, whichever of them the media information uses. Leave empty to switch the check off — there is no sensible default.

trash_age_hours.label: Untouched for at least
trash_age_hours.help: How long nothing may have changed in a folder before it can count as debris. Measured on the folder, not the files — unpacked files carry the timestamp from inside the archive, which can be years old.

trash_empty_hours.label: Empty folders already after
trash_empty_hours.help: An empty folder is unambiguously debris and does not need the full waiting time.

trash_video_mb.label: A video counts as usable from
trash_video_mb.help: If a video file of at least this size is in the folder, nothing is touched.

indexer_days.label: Period to look at
indexer_days.help: How far back the statistics are fetched from Prowlarr.

indexer_min_queries.label: Minimum queries for a judgement
indexer_min_queries.help: Below this any statement is chance, and nothing is said.

indexer_min_yield.label: Yield counts as too low below
indexer_min_yield.help: Share of queries that turned into a grab, in percent.

indexer_rank_tolerance.label: Report deviations from
indexer_rank_tolerance.help: How many places an indexer may be out of position without it being reported. With 1, five of six indexers came up in testing — pure noise.

recheck_hours.label: Report the same finding again after
recheck_hours.help: Every finding is remembered. A long-running problem reports itself again no sooner than this.

digest.label: Send a summary
digest.help: A summary of the day or the week through every notification connection: what was fixed, what is waiting for you, and whether automatic actions were paused. Skipped when there is nothing to say.

digest_day.label: Weekly summary on
digest_day.help: Only used for the weekly summary.

digest_hour.label: Send the summary at
digest_hour.help: Hour of the day, in the container's time zone (TZ).

language.label: Language
language.help: "Follow the browser" uses whatever your browser asks for.

density.label: Density
density.help: How tightly the interface is laid out.

public_url.label: Public address of this interface
public_url.help: Needed by Radarr to send the webhook here, and by Pushover for the link in the message. Behind a reverse proxy, enter the public address rather than the internal one.

log_keep.label: Findings to keep
log_keep.help: Older entries are removed. On a one minute schedule more than a thousand a day pile up easily — without a limit the store grows without bound.

log_days.label: Keep findings at most
log_days.help: In addition to the count. 0 switches the age limit off.

premature_grace_hours.label: Grace before a release counts as premature
premature_grace_hours.help: Release dates are held without a time zone and nothing comes out at midnight UTC. A day is usually right.

season_gap_min.label: Smallest gap in a season worth reporting
season_gap_min.help: One missing episode out of a finished season is worth knowing about. Raise it if your seasons are usually in flight.

blocklist_stale_days.label: Age at which a blocklist entry is questioned
blocklist_stale_days.help: Only entries for titles that are still missing are raised. Zero switches the check off.

search_attempts.label: Searches before giving up on a title
search_attempts.help: After this many fruitless searches for the same thing, the conclusion is drawn that there is no better copy out there, and it stops being searched for by itself. It is still reported, and the button still works. Zero searches for ever.

notifications_page.help: Findings are sent at the end of a run, grouped by rule, never one by one. Each connection decides for itself what it wants to hear about — an error-only push to a phone and a full log into a chat channel can sit side by side.
notifications_page.empty: No connection configured yet. Nothing is sent.
notifications_page.cooldown: Stay quiet after a message for
notifications_page.cooldown_help: Runs close together do not send twice. 0 switches it off.
notifications_page.rules_filter_help: Leave empty for all of them. A new rule is included automatically that way.
notifications_page.categories_filter_help: Leave empty for all of them.
notifications_page.telegram_no_chats: The bot has no pending messages. Write to it once in Telegram, then try again — it cannot message anyone who has not written to it first.

digest_ui.title: Summary
digest_ui.preview: What it would say right now
digest_ui.empty: Nothing happened worth a summary — nothing would be sent.

pushover.name: Pushover
pushover.help: Push to a phone. Create an application at pushover.net; the application key is shown there, the user key on your home page.

app_token.label: Application key
app_token.help: From the application you created at pushover.net.

user_key.label: User key
user_key.help: Shown on your Pushover home page.

devices.label: Devices
devices.help: Comma separated. Empty means every device.

sound.label: Sound
sound.help: The name of a Pushover sound, for example pianobar or cosmic.

telegram.name: Telegram
telegram.help: Talk to @BotFather in Telegram, create a bot and paste its token here. Then write to your bot once and press “Find chats” — a bot cannot message anyone who has not written to it first.

bot_token.label: Bot token
bot_token.help: The token @BotFather gave you, in the form 123456:ABC-DEF…

chat_id.label: Chat
chat_id.help: The chat to send to. Use “Find chats” rather than looking it up by hand.

thread_id.label: Topic
thread_id.help: Only needed for a specific topic inside a group. Leave empty otherwise.

silent.label: Send silently
silent.help: The message arrives without a sound or vibration.

discord.name: Discord
discord.help: In Discord: Server settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New webhook. Copy the webhook address and paste it here.

username.label: Shown as
username.help: The name the message appears under. Empty uses whatever the webhook is called.

avatar_url.label: Picture
avatar_url.help: Address of an image to use instead of the webhook's own.

mention.label: Mention on errors
mention.help: Only used for errors, never for anything quieter. Use the raw form, for example <@&1234> for a role.

ntfy.name: ntfy
ntfy.help: Works with ntfy.sh or your own server. Pick a topic name nobody else would guess — on a public server, anyone who knows it can read your notifications.

server.label: Server
server.help: https://ntfy.sh, or the address of your own instance.

topic.label: Topic
topic.help: On a public server this is the only thing protecting your messages. Make it long and random.

token.label: Access token
token.help: Only for a protected topic. Starts with tk_

username.label: User name
username.help: Only if your server uses a user name and password instead of a token.

password.label: Password
password.help: Goes with the user name above.

gotify.name: Gotify
gotify.help: Self-hosted. In Gotify: Apps → Create application, then copy that application's token.

server.label: Server
server.help: The address of your Gotify instance.

token.label: Application token
token.help: From the application you created in Gotify, not your client token.

webhook.name: Webhook
webhook.help: For anything else: Home Assistant, n8n, Node-RED, a script of your own. The whole report goes out as JSON, structured rather than pre-formatted, so the receiving end can do what it likes with it.

method.label: Method
method.help: POST unless the other end insists on PUT.

secret_header.label: Header name
secret_header.help: Optional. A header to send along so the receiving end can tell it is really you, for example X-Webhook-Token.

include_findings.label: Include every finding
include_findings.help: On: the full list travels with the report. Off: only the counts per rule.

welcome.title: Welcome to Correctarr
welcome.lead: Five short steps and it is running. Nothing is changed on your library until you say so.
welcome.body: Correctarr watches Radarr, Sonarr, SABnzbd and Prowlarr for the problems they notice but never resolve on their own — a download matched to the wrong film, a release that breaks a profile rule you changed afterwards, a finished file nobody could match to a title, debris left behind in the download folder.
welcome.what: What it keeps an eye on
welcome.category_queue: Downloads on their way in: wrong year, wrong title, releases that would be blocked under today's rules, ones that stopped moving.
welcome.category_import: Files that arrived but did not get in: stuck unpacking, nothing to match them to, leftover debris.
welcome.category_library: What is already on disk: unreadable files, missing audio languages, files that would not be accepted today.
welcome.category_downloader: The download client itself: warnings, a paused queue, entries whose files are long since imported.
welcome.category_indexers: Which of your indexers actually deliver, measured rather than guessed.
welcome.safety: Every rule has its own action — from report only through to correcting it — and conditions to narrow that down further. A single dry run switch stops every change at once, and it is on to begin with. The guiding principle throughout: when in doubt, do nothing.

services.title: Connect your services
services.lead: Radarr or Sonarr is required — everything else is optional and adds more checks.
services.requirement: At least one of Radarr or Sonarr has to be connected.
services.radarr: Your film library. The API key is in Radarr under Settings → General.
services.sonarr: Your series library. The API key is in Sonarr under Settings → General.
services.sabnzbd: Without it, nothing is ever classified as debris and nothing is deleted — the download client is the only thing that knows whether a folder is still in use.
services.prowlarr: Only needed for the indexer ratings. Everything else works without it.

paths.title: Where the files are
paths.lead: Paths as this container sees them, not as the host sees them.
paths.warning: This is where most setups go wrong. The paths here have to be the same ones Radarr and Sonarr see — mount the download folders exactly the way you mounted them there, or the file rules will stay quiet while there is plenty to find.

address.title: How Radarr reaches you
address.lead: Needed for the webhook that turns a delay of up to a minute into a reaction within seconds.
address.why: With this set, Radarr and Sonarr report the moment they grab something or need manual work, and a wrong download can be stopped before it finishes. Without it, everything still works — just on the schedule.
address.save: Save and set up the webhooks
address.done: Saved. Webhooks set up on {count} service(s).

notifications.title: Getting told about it
notifications.lead: Optional. You can always set this up later.
notifications.body: Findings are sent at the end of a run, grouped by rule, never one by one. Each connection decides for itself what it wants to hear about, so an error-only push to your phone and a full log into a chat channel can sit side by side.
notifications.none: Nothing is configured yet, so nothing is sent. Everything is still recorded and visible in the interface.

dry_run.title: Try it without changing anything
dry_run.lead: Strongly recommended before you let it act for the first time.
dry_run.body: With the dry run on, every rule runs and reports what it found, but nothing is touched. Look through the findings, decide whether you agree with them, then turn it off. Every rule that acts was built this way first — and every single time it turned up a mistake.

done.title: That is it
done.rules: {count} rules active, each with its own action under Rules
done.schedule: Queue checked every minute, library every 90 minutes
done.next: Have a look at Rules to see what each one does and decide which of them may act. If you left the dry run on, remember to turn it off once you are happy.

policy.heading: What should happen
policy.irreversible: This cannot be undone. Set a limit below if you want to be asked about the large ones.

action.remove_entry: Remove the entry and its folder
action.unblocklist: Take off the blocklist and search again

explain.report: Record it and leave everything alone. Always available, and always the safe answer.
explain.remove: Take it out of the queue. The same release can be grabbed again later.
explain.blocklist: Take it out of the queue and refuse this release from now on. Nothing new is searched for.
explain.blocklist_and_search: Take it out, refuse it from now on, and look for a replacement straight away.
explain.import: Bring the file into the library.
explain.import_and_clean: Bring the file in, then clear the download client entry and its source folder — the client never learns about an import done here.
explain.search: Ask the service to look for a better copy.
explain.refresh: Have the service read the file again. Often enough when the file itself is fine and only the record is stale.
explain.delete: Remove the files from disk. Only ever inside the folders configured under Paths.
explain.clear_warning: Record the warning and clear it in the download client.
explain.remove_entry: Drop the finished entry from the download client and delete its source folder.
explain.unblocklist: Removes the old blocklist entry and starts a search, so the release can be offered again.
explain.retune_profile: Sets “upgrade until custom format score” to 0. The scores still choose the best release when something is grabbed; resolution upgrades still happen.
explain.as_suggested: Each finding names its own remedy — import, blocklist, remove or nothing — from what the service says. Only remedies that are certain are carried out unasked; the rest are offered as a button.

policy.min_age_hours_help: Nothing is acted on before this much time has passed. A download that arrived two minutes ago is not stuck, it is new.
policy.max_gb_help: Anything larger is reported instead of acted on. A cheap way to say: clear the small debris, ask me about the big one.
policy.min_confidence_help: Only act when the match is at least this certain. Applies to rules that match a file to a title themselves.
policy.too_young: only {age} h old, waiting for {needed} h
policy.age_unknown: no age known for this finding
policy.too_large: {size} GB is over the limit of {limit} GB
policy.size_unknown: no size known for this finding
policy.confidence_unknown: no confidence known for this finding
policy.nothing_better: searched {tries} times already, nothing better exists
policy.failed_recently: it failed last time — trying again in {hours} h
policy.acted_too_often: acted on {count} times in {hours} h — waiting for a person
policy.regrabbed: grabbed again after it was thrown out — left alone for {hours} h, waiting for a person
policy.already_gone: it had already left the queue
policy.same_download: the same download was already dealt with in this pass
policy.managed_elsewhere: another program keeps setting this back
policy.needs_a_person: this is a matter of taste, not a fault
policy.needs_a_look: not certain enough to do unasked — offered as a button
policy.nothing_safe: nothing here would help, so nothing is done
policy.suggests_otherwise: this finding calls for something else than the configured action
policy.not_yet: nothing has been done about it yet

safety.heading: Safety limits
safety.too_many: {count} automatic actions within an hour, the limit is {limit}
safety.too_many_discards: {count} downloads or files thrown away within an hour, the limit is {limit}
safety.banner_help: Findings are still checked and reported, and buttons still work. Nothing is acted on by itself until you resume.

digest.title_daily: Correctarr today: {fixed} fixed, {waiting} waiting for you
digest.title_weekly: Correctarr this week: {fixed} fixed, {waiting} waiting for you
digest.nothing: Correctarr: nothing to report for this period
digest.failed: Tried, but it did not work

backup.skip_unknown: Not known to this version — left out.
backup.skip_needs_key: Its API key or token is not in the backup, and none is stored under this name for this address — set it up by hand.

search.nothing: nothing found in {seconds} seconds — the search may still be running, or there is nothing out there

profiles_page.name: Name of the profile
profiles_page.name_help: How it will appear in Radarr and Sonarr.
profiles_page.resolutions_help: Pick more than one and the profile will upgrade from the lower to the higher.
profiles_page.codec_help: A preference, not a requirement. x265 is about half the size at the same quality and not every device plays it.
profiles_page.audio: Lowest sound quality you will accept
profiles_page.audio_help: Everything above it is accepted too, and scored higher. Nothing below it is refused outright — it is simply worth less than an alternative.
profiles_page.languages_help: The first one you pick counts for most. Matched against the release name, where the marker actually is — including the German “DL”, which the services do not recognise by themselves.
profiles_page.language_required_label: Only grab releases in these languages
profiles_page.language_required_help: Off: preferred but not required. On: a release whose name does not say one of them is refused. Use it if you only want German.
profiles_page.size_help: Zero means no limit. Anything outside the window is refused, not merely ranked last.
profiles_page.upgrade_label: May replace a file it already has
profiles_page.upgrade_help: Only up the resolution ladder, and only once — never on score. That is what stops it grabbing the same release for ever.
profiles_page.no_services: Add Radarr or Sonarr under Services first.
profiles_page.floor_is: a release scoring below {score} is refused
profiles_page.ceiling_is: {score} — the same as the floor, so a file that was good enough to fetch is good enough to keep
profiles_page.step_is: {score} points, so two near-identical releases cannot take turns replacing each other
profiles_page.no_loops: This profile cannot cause a download loop: it never upgrades on score, only up the resolution ladder, which is finite.
profiles_page.sources_help: A disc rip and a broadcast capture at 1080p are both “1080p” and are not the same thing. Later in the list counts for more.
profiles_page.colour_help: Dolby Vision without an HDR10 layer underneath plays green on a television that does not speak it, so that combination is refused outright.
profiles_page.edition_help: A preference where more than one cut exists.
profiles_page.surround_help: 5.1 and upwards, where the release name says so.
profiles_page.streamers_help: Only a preference, and only between releases that are otherwise equal. Leave it empty if you do not mind.

profiles_ui.intro: Pick a ready profile or build your own — every choice shows what it will take on the disk before anything is written.
profiles_ui.basis_library: Sizes measured on the files in {service}.
profiles_ui.basis_reference: Sizes are reference values; with more files in {service} they are measured instead.
profiles_ui.apply_body: The profile and every custom format it needs are written into {service}.
profiles_ui.apply_note: No title is moved onto it. That is up to you, under “In the service now”.
profiles_ui.per_resolution_help: Only where one resolution should differ from the rest — HDTV only at 720p, say, or a size window that fits 2160p.
profiles_ui.rung_inherits: The same as above until you change it.
profiles_ui.upgrade_until_help: Keep a WEB-DL rather than fetch the title again when the Blu-ray comes out.
profiles_ui.loop_count: {count} of them can cause a download loop.
profiles_ui.expected: Once it has what it wants
profiles_ui.assign_help: Pick the titles. You see what it would replace and what it does to the disk before anything changes.
profiles_ui.more_titles: … and {count} more — narrow the list to see them.
profiles_ui.no_search: Nothing is searched. What the profile wants arrives when an indexer next offers it.

why.codec_required: refuses anything that does not say {codec}
why.hdr: prefers a wider range of colour
why.no_3d: refuses releases with two pictures in them
why.rubbish: refuses cam, screener, disc image and upscale
why.dv_only: refuses Dolby Vision with no HDR10 underneath — it plays green on a television that cannot read it
why.groups: prefers groups with a reputation for getting it right
why.repack: prefers a release that was put out again, fixed
why.hardcoded: refuses subtitles burned into the picture
why.retagged: refuses names that have been scrambled or stripped
why.collection: refuses a set of films when one was asked for — the service cannot import such a thing

note.language_required: Only releases whose name states {language} will be grabbed. If your indexers mostly carry other languages, little will arrive.
note.size_window: The largest file is not larger than the smallest one, so nothing can fit between them.
note.big_files: 2160p without an upper size limit can mean files of 60 GB and more.
note.x265_at_1080p: At 1080p the saving from x265 is small, and a fair number of players have to transcode it — which looks worse than the x264 it replaced.
note.dv_needs_2160p: Dolby Vision is almost only released at 2160p.
note.remux_only: Remux only means files of 30 to 80 GB and nothing else will be accepted.
note.codec_required: Only releases whose name states {codec} are taken. A release that does not name its codec at all is refused as well.

problem.no_quality: No resolution is selected, so there is nothing the profile could ever accept.
problem.cutoff_above_floor: The upgrade target ({cutoff}) is above the floor ({floor}). That is what causes download loops and is refused here.
problem.floor_too_high: The floor ({floor}) is higher than the best a release could score ({best}), so nothing would ever be grabbed.
problem.impossible_size: The smallest file ({min} GB) is not smaller than the largest ({max} GB).
problem.impossible_size_at: At {resolution} the smallest file ({min} GB) is not smaller than the largest ({max} GB), so nothing at that resolution could be taken.
problem.language_without_one: A language is required but none is selected.
problem.bad_pattern: A pattern could not be compiled: {error}
problem.no_source: No source is selected, so there is nothing the profile could ever accept.
problem.name_taken: A profile with this name already exists and was not made here. Pick another name — a profile somebody made by hand is left alone.
problem.no_such_profile: That profile does not exist on this service (any more).

film_720p.name: 720p compact
film_720p.help: Films at 720p, at most 6 GB. For a small disk or a modest player; on a large television the difference to 1080p shows.

film_1080p_compact.name: 1080p space-saving
film_1080p_compact.help: Films at 1080p up to 8 GB, x265 preferred. About half the room of a Blu-ray encode; x265 needs a player that plays it without transcoding.

film_1080p.name: 1080p balanced
film_1080p.help: Films at 1080p from WEB-DL or Blu-ray, up to 15 GB, good sound preferred. The sensible choice if you are unsure.

film_1080p_hq.name: 1080p high quality
film_1080p_hq.help: Films at 1080p with the best sound on offer, up to 30 GB. No remux.

film_2160p_hdr.name: 2160p HDR
film_2160p_hdr.help: Films at 2160p with HDR or Dolby Vision — never Dolby Vision without an HDR10 layer — and 1080p until 2160p is out. Up to 60 GB at 2160p.

film_2160p_archive.name: 2160p archive
film_2160p_archive.help: The best there is: 2160p including remux, no size limit. Expect 50 to 80 GB per film.

series_720p.name: Series 720p
series_720p.help: Series at 720p, broadcast captures included. The smallest that still looks decent.

series_1080p.name: Series 1080p
series_1080p.help: Series at 1080p from streaming or Blu-ray, and 720p for whatever never came out at 1080p — broadcast captures only at 720p. A WEB-DL is kept rather than fetched again when the Blu-ray comes out.

series_2160p.name: Series 2160p HDR
series_2160p.help: Series at 2160p with HDR, and 1080p until 2160p is out. A WEB-DL is kept rather than fetched again when the Blu-ray comes out.

anime_1080p.name: Anime 1080p
anime_1080p.help: Anime at 1080p or 720p. Subtitles are welcome, fansub releases are let in, and the group list for films and series is left out, because anime comes from different groups.

basis.service: the preferred size set in the service
basis.scaled: reference value, adjusted to your files at this resolution
basis.reference: reference value — no files of this quality to measure yet
basis.profile: measured on the files this profile already holds

outcome.assumed_kept: episodes not read one by one — assumed to stay

fits.tight: Fits only if releases stay typical in size.

outlook.unknown: Too little history to say when the disk is full.

reason.short_history: The history covers only {days} days; at least {need_days} are needed to say how fast the disk fills.
